editorial:
Imagine trying to run a circus during the chaos of World War II, but your main business isn't actually the show—it's smuggling people across borders. You get to follow Carlotta, a tough circus owner who does whatever it takes to keep her crew and her lover safe. The vibe is tense and gritty, especially when she's tasked with sneaking a famous mathematician named Professor Máté over to the partisans. Just when you think things can't get any crazier, her own son escapes from a mental asylum and joins the group, adding a layer of unpredictability and danger to every scene.

What really hits home is how the movie balances the danger of the war with the weirdness of the circus life. The acting is solid, and the tension stays high as you wonder if they will get caught by the enemy. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the payoff is worth it. If you enjoy historical dramas with a twist, you should definitely check this one out. You can grab a 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see all the detail, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: In the end, the group faces a desperate struggle to reach safety. The tension peaks as they try to get Professor Máté to the partisans while dealing with the chaos of the war around them. Some characters do not make it, showing the harsh reality of the conflict. The story wraps up by showing that while the circus was broken, the act of helping others gave them a sense of purpose and survival.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves wartime thrillers and unique character stories.
